articles.title: Stop Electing a Leader Tab. SharedWorker Just Holds the Connection.
articles.excerpt: Last week's fix for "six tabs, six WebSockets" was navigator.locks: elect one tab as leader, let it hold the one real connection, relay everything to the rest over BroadcastChannel. It works. I said a…
articles.body: Last week's fix for "six tabs, six WebSockets" was navigator.locks : elect one tab as leader, let it hold the one real connection, relay everything to the rest over BroadcastChannel . It works. I said as much at the time. It also has a seam I didn't dwell on: the connection lives inside a tab. Close that tab — the user's doing, not a bug — and the lock releases, a new leader gets picked within the same event loop turn, and that new leader still has to open a brand-new WebSocket from scratch. Real handshake, real round trip, real gap before updates resume. For a dashboard, nobody notices. For a live price ticker or a shared cursor, that gap is the whole ballgame. There's a version of this where no tab ever owns the connection, so no tab closing can take it away.
articles.author: Parsa Jiravand

articles.title: Fixing INP on Shopify stores: a practical guide for theme developers
articles.excerpt: Most Shopify performance work still focuses on load speed: compress the hero image, lazy-load below the fold, trim the app list. That matters, but it misses the metric that most often fails on real st…
articles.body: Most Shopify performance work still focuses on load speed: compress the hero image, lazy-load below the fold, trim the app list. That matters, but it misses the metric that most often fails on real stores today: Interaction to Next Paint (INP) . INP measures how quickly the page responds visually after a user does something: taps a variant swatch, opens the cart drawer, types in predictive search, clicks "Add to cart". It replaced First Input Delay as a Core Web Vital in March 2024, and it is much harder to pass, because it looks at (nearly) every interaction across the whole visit rather than only the first one. This post walks through how we find and fix INP problems on Shopify themes.

articles.title: Optimistic updates with graceful reconnect in web chat applications with React.js + TanStack Query
articles.excerpt: When working on a chat app, on any app really, it is important to take into account how the app is supposed to behave when the connection is slow or lost. The moment the user hits "send" they need to…
articles.body: When working on a chat app, on any app really, it is important to take into account how the app is supposed to behave when the connection is slow or lost. The moment the user hits "send" they need to be assured that the message is being processed instead of staring at a seemingly unresponsive page. Also, in case of a connection loss, the moment it is back on all the updates that took place in the interim must be processed immediately. This is where optimistic updates and graceful reconnect come in. First, let's talk about optimistic updates. Optimistic updates are basically when you instantly display the result of an asynchronous operation assuming it will succeed, which significantly improves perceived performance.

articles.title: TypeScript `ReadonlyMap` and `ReadonlySet` in 2026: Immutable Collections That Stop Accidental Mutation at the Type Level
articles.excerpt: TypeScript ReadonlyMap and ReadonlySet in 2026: Immutable Collections That Stop Accidental Mutation at the Type Level This article was written with the assistance of AI, under human supervision and re…
articles.body: TypeScript ReadonlyMap and ReadonlySet in 2026: Immutable Collections That Stop Accidental Mutation at the Type Level This article was written with the assistance of AI, under human supervision and review. Why ReadonlyMap and ReadonlySet Matter in 2026 Most runtime bugs in TypeScript codebases stem from unintended mutation of shared data structures. A cache gets modified during a read operation. A configuration set changes after initialization. A lookup map loses entries when a function meant to query it accidentally calls .delete() . The type system allows these mutations because developers reach for Map and Set everywhere, even when the collection should never change after construction. The solution exists at the type level.

articles.body: Earlier this week, a mass hack of refrigeration systems at an estimated 700 supermarkets throughout France caused them to suddenly malfunction, causing spoilage of untold tons of perishables and, in some cases, fires. As is now the norm, basic cybersecurity would have prevented it. French authorities say the systems, made up of entire fleets of refrigerators and freezers throughout a store, were hacked. More specifically, Internet-connected controllers that allow technicians to remotely administer the store-wide systems were compromised. The unknown attackers responsible then activated defrosters long enough for the fridges to reach temperatures as high as 50° Celsius (122° Fahrenheit).

articles.title: Planetary genealogy: Milky Way worlds belong to 1 of 2 ‘families,’ scientists find
articles.excerpt: Scientists have performed a cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems.
articles.body: You can tell a lot about how a child will age by looking at their parents, and it turns out that this could be true for planetary systems, too. Scientists have performed cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems. The study team, led by researchers at the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), studied 300 of the best-understood multiplanet systems of the over 1,000 that astronomers have discovered in the Milky Way. The team's research clarifies how the environments around infant stars directly affect planetary fates and, in turn, the survival of extrasolar planets, or exoplanets , that are potentially capable of hosting life.

articles.title: 'Dungeon Crawler Carl' author Matt Dinniman talks inspirations, success, and the upcoming Peacock TV series (interview)
articles.excerpt: 'Luckily I’m still in love with this story, and I am in love with writing it.'
articles.body: Fall has officially arrived, and as autumn leaves blaze in vivid colors, there is no better time to plunge into the imaginative world of New York Times best-selling author Matt Dinniman's "Dungeon Crawler Carl", the wildly addictive science fantasy book series that's taking the world by storm. Even if you haven't read them, you've probably seen folks carrying these books, emblazoned with their loud, neon-colored covers, at your neighborhood coffee house. You'll see it even more in the future, too, as a streaming adaptation of the novels is coming to Peacock, with Seth MacFarlane's Fuzzy Door and co-showrunners Eric Heisserer and Chris Yost at the helm.

articles.title: The AI race is back on
articles.excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg at the Meta Connect developer conference. | Photo: Andrej Sokolow/dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves,…
articles.body: Mark Zuckerberg at the Meta Connect developer conference. | Photo: Andrej Sokolow/dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves, pulling ahead with increasingly powerful models that left their rivals in the dust. Google seemed hopelessly far behind, while Meta, despite spending billions to revive its floundering AI ambitions , had yet to establish itself as a serious contender. Even the latest models coming out of China , impressive as they were, appeared to be playing catch-up. Then, in the space of a few days, everything changed. Google and Meta both unveiled frontier models they claim can go toe to toe with the best from OpenAI and Anthropic.
